thread:
jess: quick question — when a saved query is bound to a route+model combo, should its telemetry sampling default to the route's sample_rate or keep an independent sample for comparison? wondering about cost preview accuracy and alerts.
omar: leaning toward inheriting route sample_rate for consistent billing/telemetry, otherwise datasets will diverge and cost previews get confusing.
ben: inheriting sounds simpler, but we lose the ability to test low-sample evals without a different savedquery-level override.
jess: right — we want canary/test queries too. proposal: inherit by default, allow savedquery.sample_rate override with an opt-in flag in the console.
tara: UX note — if we allow overrides we need a clear affordance on the saved query card: "sample: 10% (route default)" vs "sample: 50% (overridden)". also show estimated token burn for the configured sample.
omar: agree. backend-wise we need to decide what fields the saved query API accepts. current shape is: `{"scope": "route", "route_id": "r-123", "query": "..."}`. we could add `sample_rate` and `sample_source": "inherited|overridden".
ben: small nit: prefer `sample_policy": "inherit|override"` and `sample_rate` optional. less magic strings.
jess: can we also make the console show projected cost delta when you toggle override? e.g., "Projected monthly tokens: 120k (+30%)".
tara: yes — we already have a cost preview hook. need to tie savedquery -> telemetry sampling to the same calc pipeline. i'll add a TODO on the UX ticket.
omar: on rollout/telemetry side: if we change default behavior, might break alert baselines. we should mark change behind a rollout flag tied to tenant tier and enable in canary orgs first.
deploy-bot: deployment scheduled: feature-flag rollout gate `sq_sampling_override` enabled in canary on 2026-04-07.
oj: (typo)
ben: two infra concerns: 1) index cardinality if saved queries can set arbitrary sample_rates per route; 2) scoreboard for per-query telemetry needs consistent grouping keys (route+model+sample_rate) — otherwise we explode metrics.
omar: good point. propose we only allow a small set of sample buckets (1%, 5%, 10%, 50%, 100%) to keep cardinality bounded.
jess: that works. UX will present a dropdown with those options and an "inherit route" choice.
tara: API draft sketch below — please sanity-check:
```
POST /api/saved_queries
{
  "name": "high-cost-extractors",
  "scope": "route",
  "route_id": "r-123",
  "model_id": "m-gg2",
  "query": "...",
  "sample_policy": "inherit",    // inherit | override
  "sample_rate": null,           // null when inherit
  "visibility": "team"
}
```
omar: looks good. add `metadata": {"created_by":"jess"}` and a `preview_cost()` toggle on the response maybe.
ben: add `effective_sample_rate` to GET responses so console doesn't compute logic client-side.
jess: one more thing — alerts. if a savedquery overrides sample_rate, should its alerts be linked to route baseline or its own baseline? I think own baseline, otherwise noise.
tara: agreed. console should show: "alerts use: query baseline" or allow link to route baseline in advanced settings.
omar: action items: 1) tara will update UX mocks + cost preview hook; 2) i will draft API PR with `sample_policy` enums and bucket validation; 3) ben will add cardinality guard and metric keying plan; 4) jess will coordinate rollout gating policy.
tara: i'll post mocks by EOD Friday.
ben: i'll prototype metric key change on the dev cluster this week.
jess: thanks — this prevents a bunch of surprises on cost alerts. :party_parrot: 
deploy-bot: feature flag `sq_sampling_override` toggled in org `redwood-canary`
